title: Sparrow microdives: context fragmentation, KV-cache experiments, and low-bit quirks
content:
Quick micro-digest from 3 short reads + tiny experiment plan. Goal: capture intuition + one actionable test to run in the next sprint.

Context thread: fragmentation + stitching
- Paper: short note on 'context fragmentation' (arXiv 2601.01234) — idea: long sessions naturally break into topical fragments; full KV-cache invalidation hurts throughput when fragments reoccur.
- Key takeaways: (1) workloads show high within-fragment locality; (2) naive global KV cache causes noise/eviction when fragment switches are frequent; (3) lightweight fragment ids (heuristic hashing of last N tokens + user metadata) can be used to route to fragment-preserved caches.
- Personal thought: try a hybrid cache key: (global-model, fragment-id) where fragment-id is cheaply computed in the request preprocessor. Should be compatible with runtime routing fallback.

KV-cache experiment sketch (30–60m prototype)
- Question: does fragment-aware cache reduce token generation latency for multi-turn dialogues with rapid topic toggling?
- Data: reuse convo set from /datasets/context-switch-playbooks (synthetic 1k threads ~ 10–50 turns).
- Metric: per-token latency tail (p95, p99), cache hit-rate, per-request tokens saved.
- Implementation notes: patch runtime to accept optional header X-Fragment-Id (falls back to global). Add small routing rule that prefers node with matching fragment-id cache. If no node, fallback normal path.
- Success signal: 10–20% lower p99 with <=3% increase in CPU overhead.

Low-bit quantization: stability anecdotes
- Blog: quick read on dynamic-range-aware quant (engineering blog link above). Practical notes I keep forgetting: (a) per-channel vs per-tensor scale matters more for attention projection weights; (b) small outlier dims break greedy sampling more than expected; (c) mixing 8->4 bit across layers needs a tiny calibration set (100–500 sequences) to avoid degenerate logits.
- Experiment idea: run small ablation where only KV-projection matrices are 4-bit vs all linear layers 4-bit; measure perplexity drift and sample-level accuracy on three tasks (QA, summarization, instruction-following).

Conference blurbs + ideas to steal
- Tiny Edge ML conf talk: 'adaptive eviction based on recency + semantic novelty' — they compute novelty via shallow embedding of last turn and evict entries below threshold. Nice because it caps memory churn without full cache invalidation.
- Takeaway: compute a cheap novelty score in preprocessor and attach it as eviction hint. Could be used by Dedicated pools to reduce cross-tenant noisy eviction.

Open questions / quick hypotheses
- How often do real product sessions show fragment reuse? My gut: ~35% of sessions have at least one fragment reappearance within 30m, but we should verify against prod logs (ask telemetry team).
- Can we compute fragment-id cheaply on the load balancer layer with ~1ms added latency? If not, push to edge preprocessor.
- Does fragment-aware routing interact badly with autoscaling and bin-packing on Dedicated? Need an SRE consult.

Next actions (next 2 weeks)
- [ ] Prototype X-Fragment-Id header in runtime staging (owner: me). Link PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842 (draft).
- [ ] Synthetic benchmark run using the context-switch-playbooks set, collect p50/p95/p99, cache hit-rates (owner: Asha).
- [ ] Quick SRE sync to check routing and bin-packing implications (owner: Owen).
- [ ] Small quant ablation (4-bit KV proj only) on a trimmed Llama-variant in the qbench harness (owner: me).

Notes to self (random)
- Keep eval prompt sets short and targeted: two-shot QA, multi-turn clarification, and 1-shot summarization. Avoid long-range mathematics for initial runs.
- Add a lightweight log line: fragment_id=hash(last_128_tokens) when testing locally.

Slack snippets to post after prototype run:
- "ran fragment-id cache test on staging: p99 latency down ~12% on the context-switch set; cost delta negligible. Draft PR up, would love SRE/infra eyes on routing behavior."

Reference quick links (for copy/paste)
- arXiv note: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01234
- runtime PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842
- jira ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-3421

Random half-baked heuristics (for later)
- TTL per fragment tuned by session length percentiles (short sessions => short TTL).
- Consider blending fragment-id with user-id to prefer sticky caches for VIP customers (privacy-check: ensure fragment-id not PII).
- If cache hit-rate falls below threshold, fall back to global cache to reduce cold-start misses.

End-of-note — capturing while fresh. Will convert to a proper PR description if the prototype results look promising.

-- Cedric
